items.title: Operator Room Vancouver: Cash Flow, Demand Planning, and Scaling Past $30M, Dee Agarwal, Tony Yu, Bryce Alderson, Lucinda Holland
items.description:
In this Operator Room Vancouver, four operators (Dee Agarwal/AMA Holdings and Goli, Tony Yu/Vessi, Bryce Alderson/Nutratology, Lucinda Holland/Sacheu Beauty) discuss the real operating problems that show up once a brand scales past tens of millions in revenue: cash flow crises, demand planning failures, pricing architecture, and hiring philosophy, followed by live teardowns of an Amazon listing, a Shopify store, and a TikTok Shop.

 

TOPICS:

  1. Real cash flow and demand planning failures at scale: a $1.6M GST refund held hostage by a tax audit, tariff-driven manufacturing lead time shocks, and repeated TikTok Shop-driven stockouts, plus the specific fixes (negative cash conversion cycles, revolving credit lines, 15-day lead times) each brand now uses.
  2. Pricing and unit economics philosophy: why one operator refuses to grow unprofitably and uses strict line pricing, while another argues Amazon-only sellers should exploit flexible pricing architecture (testing price/TACOS combinations) since they're not bound by retail price matching.
  3. Live teardowns of a real Amazon listing (trailer hitches), Shopify store (plants), and TikTok Shop (nail files/beauty), plus closing Q&A on AI/GEO visibility tactics and each panelist's hiring and firing philosophy.

items.title: Build Your Own 24/7 AI Employee － Shawn Kolodny － SoFlo Chapter AI Boardroom July 2026
items.description:
In this session, Shawn Kolodny (Big Shiny Balls, a made-to-order giant inflatables company) walks through how he built and runs "Sam Clawson," an always on OpenClaw based AI agent that handles outbound email, reporting, Zendesk, ClickUp, and more, including a costly lesson from giving it too much access too fast.

 

TOPICS:

  1. The practical setup: running the agent from a Mac Mini (or a portable setup while traveling), connecting it to Slack channels split by topic to avoid context bleed, and using Notion as its central memory and database.
  2. Permissions and guardrails: starting with read-only access and expanding gradually, since giving an inexperienced agent broad write access (in his case, to his Shopify site's code) caused real damage to SEO and site stability.
  3. Why writing a "soul" file with beliefs rather than a rigid rules checklist made the agent feel more like a working partner than a compliance bot, plus the daily cron jobs (sales reports, rush order alerts, ticket triage) now running the business in the background.

items.title: How to Give Claude Perfect Memory － Ramon Gonzalez － SoFlo Chapter AI Boardroom July 2026
items.description:
In this session, Ramon Gonzalez explains why Claude Code sessions seem to "forget" or contradict earlier instructions, and walks through the memory architecture he built to fix it: split memory files, nightly and weekly summarization agents, and a searchable company wiki.


TOPICS:

  1. Why a single CLAUDE.md file quietly fails: it only loads the first 200 lines into a session even if you've written 400 or 500, so important information written past that line simply never gets read.
  2. His fix: splitting memory by subject (PPC, listings, B2B, etc.) so each session only loads what's relevant, plus a two-step nightly and weekly agent process that condenses daily conversation logs into a clean, non-contradictory main memory file.
  3. A company wiki (built using Google's Open Knowledge Format) that sits between memory and live data search, effectively functioning as machine-readable SOPs that any employee's own Claude instance can reference consistently.

items.title: Hot Seat: Disclosing AI Generated Images Under New York Law － Natascha Moreno － SoFlo Chapter AI Boardroom July 2026
items.description:
In this quick hot seat, Natascha Moreno flags a new New York law requiring disclosure whenever an ad contains an AI-generated ("synthetic") performer, and shares a free tool that adds that disclosure to images in bulk.

 

TOPICS:

  1. The New York law's requirement that any advertisement containing a synthetic performer include a clear disclosure, and why the group is surprised this appears to cover static images, not just video.
  2. Why this applies broadly, including Amazon listing images, since any brand selling to customers in New York is potentially in scope, not just brands headquartered there.
  3. A walkthrough of GenRupt, a free tool that batch adds a customizable disclosure label to up to 100 images at once, as a faster alternative to manually editing in tools like Canva or ChatGPT.

items.title: Hot Seat: Where to Apply AI on a New Amazon Account － Alex Castillo － SoFlo Chapter AI Boardroom July 2026
items.description:
In this short hot seat, Alex Castillo, who secured exclusive Amazon representation for a new lipstick brand, asks the group where AI can help him run the account, and the group narrows it down to PPC and inventory management, with a side debate on AI video ads.

 

TOPICS:

  1. Why the group recommends focusing AI specifically on PPC and inventory management as the highest value starting points for a new, inexperienced Amazon seller.
  2. A disagreement over AI-generated video ads: effective for Amazon's video and search ad placements at scale, but riskier for wellness and beauty brands where customers expect a more human touch and can react negatively.
  3. Quick context on price point and order volume for a premium lipstick brand versus other members' businesses, highlighting how differently "high AOV, low volume" categories operate.

items.title: 60 Days. 2 SKUS. Zero Paid Placements － Boris Ermis － SoFlo Chapter AI Boardroom July 2026
items.description:
In this session, Boris Ermis (launching MSK Labs, a new beauty brand with a celebrity spray tan artist co-founder) shows how organic PR, not paid media, generated retail buyer interest, VC calls, and Amazon spillover within the brand's first 60 days.

 

TOPICS:

  1. How one PR driven event (a hotel suite with free spray tans for a dozen top beauty editors) led to coverage in major beauty publications, and why that press mattered more than paid ads at launch.
  2. How press coverage snowballed unprompted into retail buyer outreach (Violet Gray, Blue Mercury), inbound VC interest (sourced from a niche beauty investment newsletter), and cheap, high-converting Amazon and Meta traffic.
  3. A separate story about using Claude to scrape and translate Farsi Telegram channels during the Iran conflict to time an oil short, offered as an aside on unconventional AI use cases.

items.title: How I Automated My Amazon PPC Account － Michael Benlolo － SoFlo Chapter AI Boardroom July 2026
items.description:
In this session, Michael Benlolo explains how he replaced two PPC hires (an agency and a VA) with a Claude-built automation system managing 900 campaigns across 168 ASINs, cutting his TACOS by 58 percent over five months.

 

TOPICS:

  1. Why he fired his PPC agency and VA the same day he got access to Claude, betting he could rebuild the function himself through structured automation rather than manual account management.
  2. His system architecture: strategy documented first, Claude used to write fixed scripts (not freeform agents) for daily bid, budget, and inventory-driven ad spend decisions, with weekly WhatsApp approval for riskier actions like negative keywords.
  3. A genuinely novel feature no PPC software offers: automatically throttling and shutting off ad spend based on real time days of inventory remaining, rather than letting campaigns run regardless of stock levels.

items.title: Staying Human at Machine Speed － Eli Elias － SoFlo Chapter AI Boardroom July 2026
items.description:
In this session, Eli Elias shares five AI automations he built for his cannabis-to-supplement manufacturing brand, then pivots into a candid warning about what heavy AI use is doing to him personally: disrupted sleep, eroding social skills, and blurred boundaries between man and machine.


TOPICS:

  1. Five production automations built with his brother (a top-tier coder): an SEO content engine, a product formulation and quoting tool, a Shopify fraud/fulfillment agent that replaced a VA, and an early-stage customer persona testing tool.
  2. Adoption statistics suggesting most companies using AI aren't seeing real benefit, and his argument that the gap is mostly about how deliberately the operator uses it.
  3. The personal cost of round-the-clock AI use: sleep debt from late-night building sessions, atrophying social skills, outsourcing ethical judgment to a tool with "no soul," and concrete boundaries he now uses to protect his time and mental health (time-boxed builds, yoga, scheduled human connection).

items.title: Organizing Potential Events more Efficiently － Penina First － SoFlo Chapter AI Boardroom July 2026
items.description:
In this short session, Penina First (who recently sold a GPS dog walking company, now launching a new ecommerce brand) shares a simple Claude- and Gmail-based system she built to stop event invitations from overwhelming her calendar while she balances learning with actually building her new business.


TOPICS:

  1. Connecting Gmail to Claude with a "potential events" label and inbox rule so invitations from event organizers (MDS, Startup CPG, trade shows, etc.) get automatically filtered and categorized rather than lost in her inbox.
  2. Having Claude sort events into virtual, in-person nearby, and in-person elsewhere, viewable on a dashboard or delivered as a daily draft email digest of new and upcoming events.
  3. A brief tangent on MDS's own in-development AI tool, a WhatsApp-connected assistant trained on member chats, event transcripts, and databases that can answer questions about relevant events and resources.

items.title: Building Scalable Amazon Operations with Data Automation, Clean Databases, and AI －Dorian Gorski －Mogul Call
items.description:
In this session, Dorian Gorski discusses the creation of a closed-loop system for business automation using a structured database approach, emphasizing the equal importance of both business and operational data.

TOPICS:

  1. The approach to building reliable business automations using a tiered database structure (bronze, silver, and gold) combined with Python to prevent AI errors.
  2. The distinction and integration between business intelligence (quantitative data) and operational intelligence (qualitative data like SOPs and tasks).
  3. The process of implementing automations with a human-in-the-loop initially, capturing data receipts from decisions, and continuously optimizing workflows through feedback.
